slot.subtopic: Magnetic field due to finite wire / polygon loop
slot.brief: Magnetic field at centre of a regular polygonal coil (square/hexagon) of N turns with current I; direct superposition formula or comparison of square vs circular loop of same perimeter.

stem: A square coil and a circular coil each have $N$ turns, carry the same current $I$, and have equal perimeters. What is the ratio of the magnetic field magnitude at the square coil's centre to that at the circular coil's centre?

verdicts.working: For square side a, B_s = 2√2 μ₀NI/(πa). Equal perimeters give circular radius R = 2a/π, so B_c = μ₀NI/(2R) = πμ₀NI/(4a). Therefore B_s/B_c = 8√2/π².

working:
For square side $a$, $B_{\square}=4N\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi(a/2)}(2\sin45^\circ)=\dfrac{2\sqrt2\mu_0NI}{\pi a}$. Equal perimeter gives $R_{\circ}=2a/\pi$, so $B_{\circ}=\dfrac{\mu_0NI}{2R_{\circ}}=\dfrac{\pi\mu_0NI}{4a}$. Thus $\dfrac{B_{\square}}{B_{\circ}}=\dfrac{8\sqrt2}{\pi^2}$.

Independent check: For square side a, B_s = 2√2 μ₀NI/(πa). Equal perimeters give circular radius R = 2a/π, so B_c = μ₀NI/(2R) = πμ₀NI/(4a). Therefore B_s/B_c = 8√2/π².
solution:
For a square of side $a$, the field at the centre is $B_s=\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}\mu_0NI}{\pi a}$. Equal perimeters give the circular coil radius $R=\dfrac{2a}{\pi}$, hence $B_c=\dfrac{\mu_0NI}{2R}=\dfrac{\pi\mu_0NI}{4a}$. Therefore,
$$\frac{B_s}{B_c}=\frac{8\sqrt{2}}{\pi^2}$$
